messages.author: 50200f3ca6d68cad
messages.subject: error message in growth()
parts:
Hello

I am trying to fit a conditional latent growth model to my data, using an ordinal variable (Family) to predict change in another variable (ATT):

'
LG_ATT <- '


ATT1 =~ 1*AtitudesP_a + a*AtitudesP_b + b*AtitudesP_c
ATT2 =~ 1*Atitudes_a + a*Atitudes_b + b*Atitudes_c


AtitudesP_a ~ 0*1
Atitudes_a ~ 0*1


ATT1 ~ 0*1
ATT2 ~ 0*1


AtitudesP_b ~ w*1
AtitudesP_c ~ z*1
Atitudes_b ~ w*1
Atitudes_c ~ z*1


AtitudesP_a ~~ Atitudes_a
AtitudesP_b ~~ Atitudes_b
AtitudesP_c ~~ Atitudes_c


Intercept =~ 1*ATT1 + 1*ATT2
LinearSlope =~ 0*ATT1 + 1*ATT2


Intercept + LinearSlope ~ Family
'


I had previously formatted the 'Family' variable like this:

mydata$Family <- factor(mydata$Family, levels = c("1","2","3"), ordered = T)


when I fit the model to the data I get this message

LG_ATT_EST <- growth(LG_ATT, data=mydata, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml")
Error in if (is.finite(fx) && fx < 0) fx <- 0 : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Is the problem with the data, or have I made a mistake in the above code? mydata$Family contains no NAs. 


Thanks in advance for any help!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: error message in growth()
parts: an ordinal variable (Family) to predict

Ordinal-variable models are only available for ordinal outcomes.  Ordinal / nominal predictors must be modeled using dummy codes

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

The lavaan() defaults in the growth() wrapper are meant for observed indicators of growth, not latent indicators (i.e., curve of factors models).  Just use the lavaan() function and make sure your syntax specifies all nonzero parameters.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

If you have an exogenous ordinal variable, you can use a coding scheme reflecting the order (say, 1,2,3,…) and treat it as any other (numeric) covariate.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: error message in growth()
parts: If I understand correctly, I can simply change my "Family" factor variable to a numerical variable? I had tried this before and the results seemed great, I just thought I should use an ordinal factor.

Using dummy codes, you can treat it as a nominal variable.  Then you can calculate the means and test a linearity hypothesis using constraints (or using the new support in semTools for the emmeans package).  If the Family factor is your only predictor of growth, you could also treat it as a nominal factor by running a multigroup model.
Sorry if I misunderstood, but does that mean I cannot use the growth() function for second-order latent growth modeling?
You misunderstood, my comment had nothing to do with second-order growth models.  It was only a question of how to treat an ordinal predictor.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
